goalInOwnWords: Turn scrap into as much money as possible over six shifts by adding machines to a line, fill the order each shift so every price goes up, and finish ahead of the foreman's total.
stoppedWhere: On a second game on a practice yard, straight after the first shift's report ($888, 'add a hopper'), then Menu, Save and go home, then the feedback form. (All three lessons were done yesterday; I did none today. Today's yard was played to the end first: three stars, $18,730.)
stoppedWhy: I got what I came for: a clear sum I could work out myself, three stars, and I beat Sal by $2,635. The second board opened with the exact same $888 shift and the exact same sentence under it, so I could see how the rest would go: the same ladder of machines with the furniture moved. And I did not fancy the Turn-button dance again. I would come back for tomorrow's yard, not grind a second board tonight.

stuck.where: Shift 1 of today's yard, turning the second furnace
stuck.what: Which end of the furnace was in and which was out, and which way the Turn button rotates; the little orange and blue marks are tiny and I could not read them.
stuck.gotOutHow: Pressed Turn again and again, watching Sal's 'This piece leads nowhere' line and the 'This shift will pay' figure until the line was accepted and the figure went up.

stuck.where: Shifts 2 and 4, placing a new crusher
stuck.what: In shift 2 the first square I tried was a heap of junk and the crusher would not stay there; in shift 4 a tip said the crusher only takes things from behind and nothing fed it there, which I had no way of knowing until I had put it down.
stuck.gotOutHow: The tips said why ('That's a junk pile. Nothing can stand here: go around it', 'Tap it to turn it'), so I moved the machine to another square and turned it to face where I wanted.

stuck.where: Shift 1 of the second yard, the belt round the corner
stuck.what: The belt curved itself into the other furnace instead of on to the crate box, and the forecast stayed at $576.
stuck.gotOutHow: Pressed Turn on the belt and added one more belt; the forecast went to $888.

confused: 'Lit spots: off' on the job card: I remembered the game lighting up squares yesterday and could not tell whether 'off' was how things stood now or what a tap would do, nor why they were off.
The word 'practice' beside 'Today's yard' in the top corner: I did not know if that game counted (the results page later treated it as a real game).
Which end of a machine is in and which is out (tiny orange and blue marks), and which way Turn rotates it.
The 25% rise is 25% of the original price each time ($24, then $30, then $36), not 25% on top of the new price, which is how the card can be read; I had to work that out from the price list.
Whether the Plate Press takes shards from the side: the crusher's tip said it only takes things from behind, so I expected the press to be the same (it is not).
What 'You're level with Sal' is compared against in the early shifts, since the figure on the job card is Sal's whole-game total.
annoyed: Pressing Turn several times to face a machine the right way, on both yards.
After dropping a piece the right-hand panel rearranged itself, so a tap where Turn had been hit 'Buy a belt: $20' and my total fell from $888 to $868 with no 'are you sure' (Undo gave it back).
Every shift report hands over the cure as well as the diagnosis ('add a hopper', 'a Tuner touching it would clear it'); I would rather have only the diagnosis and work out the cure.
The second yard's first shift was identical to the first yard's, to the dollar and the sentence under it.
No way to tell if $18,730 is a good score beyond beating Sal; there is no board in this version.
pleased: The 'This shift will pay $X' figure before pressing Start was exact: every shift of the first game paid to the dollar what it promised, so I came to trust the numbers.
The shift report is a ledger I can check: '74 x ingot @ $36 = $2,664', plus 'What held you back' with a red tag on the machine itself.
The 'What things sell for' list with the machine times let me work out the right card from the numbers, with nobody telling me.
'Put the Furnace where you think. The pay shows if it helps.' leaves the solving to me.
Tips that say why: 'That's a junk pile. Nothing can stand here: go around it', 'Furnace points out of the yard. Tap it to turn it.'
Belts turn corners by themselves, a hopper turns to face its crusher, and a placed machine can be dragged to a new square.
The results page: three stars, 'You beat Sal by $2,635', 'Since yesterday: $9,840 ... $18,730 today (+$8,890)', and a new rank.
bestMoment: Dropping the Tuner on the belt square that touched both furnaces and watching the forecast go from $1,764 to $2,664, a square I worked out myself, and then the shift paid exactly $2,664.
worstMoment: Tapping where Turn had been and finding $20 gone because the panel had moved under my finger.
oneChange: Make each yard a different puzzle: the second board opened with the identical $888 shift and the same advice, so I could see the whole game; if each yard changed what the numbers want, I would open it every morning.
